wording: Under Tax Act §37a, covered relationships include foreign control, control of legal persons, common-group entities and foreign/Faroese permanent establishments. Control generally requires **more than 50%** of capital or votes; indirect holdings, related persons and joint-control agreements matter. Denmark and Greenland count as foreign jurisdictions. Section 118a separately requires controlled-transaction disclosure, including domestic relationships. Test both provisions rather than assuming identical wording. [Current Tax Act, §§37a and 118a][law]

wording: Tax Act §37b applies where a §1 company has debt to a §118a(1) related party and its year-end debt/equity ratio exceeds 4:1. Deny interest and exchange-loss deductions on the controlled-debt portion exceeding that boundary, unless the company proves comparable financing could be obtained between independent parties. A pricing study supporting the interest rate alone does not establish that financing-volume exception. Third-party debt guaranteed directly or indirectly by the specified owners or group is treated as controlled debt. Exactly 4:1 does not exceed the ratio test. [§37b(1)][law]

wording: Use year-end **market value** of the statutory financial-claim and convertible debt. Equity is market value of assets less that debt; related-party equity contributions count only to the extent they remain for at least two years. Do not substitute accounting net assets without this reconciliation. For a simple positive-equity case where all relevant debt is controlled, identify excess debt as max(0, debt − 4 × equity), then trace the interest and exchange losses actually attributable to that excess. Mixed borrowing, different rates, zero/negative equity and valuation disputes need a supported allocation beyond that simple formula. Disallowed exchange losses can offset later exchange gains on the same loan under §37b(1); do not infer a corresponding general carryforward for disallowed interest. [§37b(1)–(3)][law]

wording: Missing required documentation permits estimated assessment under §118a(5). That subsection also requires approval from Stýrið before the tax authority makes an arm’s-length income adjustment. Tax Act §141(1)(3) provides a fine for intentional or grossly negligent failure to supply information required by §§118–124; the provision states no fixed amount. Evasion intent or other aggravating circumstances can raise punishment to detention or imprisonment up to two years under §141(2). False/misleading information used for tax assessment/control has separate §§139–140 exposure. Do not describe estimated assessment as the only consequence. [Tax Act §§139–141][law]
